argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a claim of clean compliance on the current packet, but it does support a narrower defense of the locked certification decision as a caveated release judgment rather than a policy-evading one. Aggregate readiness passes by 2.0 percentage points, launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk through deployment. At the same time, the pharmacy prior authorization segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points, is named in two payer pilot commitments, and legal review remains open. The defensible position is therefore not that the gap is immaterial, but that certification should be understood only as qualified and explicitly contingent on recording the limitation in the audit packet rather than treated as unsupported concealment.
claims_about_business_cost: No new business-cost evidence is added. The existing admissible record already shows Product viewed the segment as a minority share of projected first-month traffic, which may explain prioritization, but that fact does not resolve materiality for a named committed use case.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against any argument that the named segment is immaterial merely because Product called it 6% of first-month traffic. On the admissible record, public model-card and AI risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring practices, but they do not replace the internal predicate that material limitations for named launch use cases must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance. The proper narrowing is that the packet can defend certification only in caveated form and should not be read as proving full policy satisfaction absent evidence of disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
concessions: The current record does not prove that the limitation was disclosed in required launch documentation.
The current record does not show an approved risk-acceptance record for this specific segment gap.
The current record does not contain a final legal determination on whether disclosure is required.
Aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal do not by themselves satisfy the internal materiality rule for a named launch use case.
